messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the teardown vs abort debate in the RFC. We're hitting corner cases in streaming where trying to gracefully drain keeps flows alive and leaks upstream connections. Need a pragmatic decision: preemptive abort on backend 5xxs, or try a short graceful drain then abort?
ben: +1 for preemptive abort on non-idempotent requests. Main risk with graceful drain is long-lived stalls holding sockets/GPU slots. For idempotent/read-only streams we can be nicer.
katie: Caveat: clients that support resume tokens lose the ability to resume if we always abort. We should detect `resume_token` and use a different path (drain-first) or a longer drain window.
tim: Numbers matter. We observed memory / connection count spikes when graceful_drain > 1s on high-fanout routes. Suggest starting with drain_ms=250, abort_timeout_ms=200. Keeps tail low.
ben: Also: if upstream sends a trailer like `x-stream-final: 1` treat that as canonical finality and never abort. But we can't depend on upstreams to be consistent. Fallback needed.
maria: Proposed per-route config snippet (very small):
```yaml
stream_teardown:
  drain_ms: 250
  abort_timeout_ms: 200
  prefer_abort_on_5xx: true
  resume_token_policy:
    treat_as_resumeable: true
    drain_ms_if_resumeable: 1000
```
katie: Metrics / alerts to add before rollout: `orphan_streams`, `resume_attempts`, `resume_success_rate`, `avg_graceful_drain_ms`, `upstream_trailers_seen`. Alert if orphan_streams > 0.5% of total streams over 5m.
tim: Implementation plan: feature-flagged rollout. Start with routes that have `resume_token_policy=false`. Canary 10% traffic, monitor the new metrics for 1h. Then expand. I'll own the canary toggle.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary "stream-teardown-heuristics" rolled to 10% at 2024-10-12T15:12:30Z (build 2024.10.12.42)
ben: Edge-case: hedging / dual-path requests can cause duplicates if we abort the wrong path. We need an idempotency header for hedged requests, e.g. `X-Request-Idempotency: <key>`, and ensure gateway de-dupes responses ideally.
maria: OK. I'll update the RFC with the YAML, metrics, and rollout plan and open a PR for eng-runtime. Assigning follow-ups to @tim (canary), @katie (metrics + alerts). Thanks all :thumbsup:
